title: What Glorious Tidings Do I Hear
description: What Glorious Tidings Do I Hear in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Sebastian Streeter wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 256 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Blessings of the Gospel”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: What glo-rious ti-dings do I hear From my Re-deem-er's tongue! I can no lon-ger si-lence bear; I'll burst in-to a song:

lines: What glorious tidings do I hear
I can no longer silence bear;
The blind receive their sight with joy;
The dumb their loosened tongues employ;
The deaf can hear the word.
The dead are raised to life anew
The glorious gospel's preached to you,
O wondrous type of things divine,
To raise from woe the sinking mind

licence: Public domain: Sebastian Streeter died in 1867.
credits: Words by Sebastian Streeter (1783–1867), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
